cohort: The study included two million term children from Danish national registries, born between 1977 and 2012.
finding: Children delivered by cesarean section had significantly increased risk of asthma, systemic connective tissue disorders, juvenile arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, immune deficiencies, and leukemia.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with increased risks for several chronic immune diseases, but not with type 1 diabetes, psoriasis, or celiac disease.
